default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-898.title: Rolling-median cross follow
E-898.hypothesis: The rolling median ignores single-bar spikes; a close crossing it marks a durable shift in where trades clear, which trend followers and stop orders then extend.

E-899.title: Negative-autocorrelation regime fade
E-899.hypothesis: When recent bar returns alternate in sign (market making dominates), a large bar is mostly liquidity taking that gets reverted; fade it only in that regime.

E-900.title: Staircase failure
E-900.hypothesis: After several consecutive higher highs and higher lows, a close below the previous low shows the trend buyers stopped; late trend followers exit into it and the move extends.

E-901.title: Prior-close dwell cross
E-901.hypothesis: The previous session's close is the reference for overnight holders and gap traders; after dwelling on one side, a close across it signals a change of sentiment versus yesterday.

E-902.title: Day-open re-cross after an excursion
E-902.hypothesis: After a stretch away from the open, a close back through it means the excursion was fully retraced and its late participants are trapped; follow the reversal.

E-903.title: Absorption bar break
E-903.hypothesis: Heavy volume with a small range means one side absorbed the other's orders; the next bar's break of the absorption bar shows which side ran out.

E-905.title: Force-index zero cross
E-905.hypothesis: Price change times volume weights moves by participation; the smoothed series changing sign marks money flow switching side and momentum traders joining.

E-906.title: Reversal after range expansion
E-906.hypothesis: A bar several times wider than recent bars that closes near its extreme against the prior drift is a capitulation of the trend side; trapped positions fuel the reversal.

E-907.title: One-sided bar-colour saturation fade
E-907.hypothesis: When nearly every recent bar has the same colour the move is crowded and thinly supplied by the other side; the first saturated reading precedes a pause or pullback, so fade it.

E-904.title: Index surge, dollar fades (WDO)
E-904.hypothesis: A sharp index move with dollar inversely correlated means foreign-flow hedgers lag; the dollar follows opposite to the index surge.
